newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan September consumer prices up 3.84 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan September consumer prices up 3.84 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's September consumer prices rose 3.84 percent compared to a year earlier, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Saturday.
On a month-to-month basis, the September consumer price index was down 0.55 percent from August, the directorate said.
At the wholesale level, September wholesale prices were down 3.29 percent from September 1995 and down 0.30 percent from August 1996.

Directorate economists attributed the slowing rate of rise in the consumer price index to the market's gradual recovery from a spate of typhoons that seriously damaged Taiwan crops in July and August and sent vegetable and fruit prices soaring.
Taiwan had had no major typhoons in the same period of 1995, skewing the year-on-year comparison for September, they said.
The agency said September saw a sharp 21.62 percent decline in vegetable prices in September compared to August as new post-typhoon crops flowed into the market.
The vegetable price decreases contributed to a 3.12 percent decline in overall food prices in September from August.

Despite dramatic storm-related upticks in food prices in August, consumer prices in the first nine months of 1996 rose at an average of 3.05 percent per month, well below the state's second-half target of 3.5 percent CPI growth.
In August, the agency forecast that consumer prices were on track to climb 3.33 percent for all of calendar 1996.
